_comment: Register-exclusion list for the maxDF* corpus-convergence metric. These are NEX5's OWN habitual vocabulary -- the words her crystallized voice uses regardless of subject. They are excluded so that maxDF* measures convergence onto an EXTERNAL topic, not the standing register. This list is FITTED DATA and it WILL DRIFT. Refit when 'fitted_on' is stale, and refit ONLY on a corpus with no active convergence in it.
method: document frequency over the corpus using _fidelity_tokens() from crystallizer.py (GENIUS_FIDELITY_BASELINE.md section 1: lowercase, strip possessives, drop <3 chars, drop furniture); take the top 40 by DF
stability_check: refitting with the last 7 or 14 days withheld keeps 33/40 terms and leaves the backtest quantiles identical (12/18/22%), so the metric is not sensitive to the exact tail of this list

correction.what: Removed 2 of the original 40 terms: 'changes' and 'systems'.
correction.why: This list was fitted 2026-06-20..2026-08-04, a window that spans the 'Gatwick' exemplar-pool contamination (fires 2026-07-26..2026-08-07, crystallized beliefs 2026-07-28..2026-08-08). That violates this file's own header rule -- 'refit ONLY on a corpus with no active convergence in it'. Three contaminant tokens sat in the 40: changes, shifts, systems. Measured against a clean pre-contamination corpus (2026-06-01..2026-07-28, n=1627, 0 contaminant): 'changes' DF 0.0080 and 'systems' DF 0.0197, NEITHER in a clean top-40 -- they entered this list only because of the contamination, and excluding them blinds maxDF* to any future convergence driven by them. 'shifts' was KEPT: DF 0.0301 clean, rank 37 in a clean fit, so it is genuine standing register.
correction.measured_effect_on_readings: NONE. Replaying maxDF* daily over 2026-07-01..2026-08-10 with and without these two terms gives an identical breach history (1 breach day, peak 30.0% on 08-04 driven by 'societal') and an identical mean live reading (19.5%). The contamination of this list was real but INERT: the tokens it wrongly absorbed never drove a reading. This correction buys future sensitivity, not a changed past.
correction.what_was_NOT_done: A full refit was rejected on measurement. A clean corpus large enough for a stable 40-term fit exists (2026-06-01..2026-07-28, n=1627; bootstrap shows ~1000 docs needed for R31's 33/40 stability bar), but it is entirely PRE-R29. Refitting on it is a REGRESSION for live use: it drops 'emerging' (DF 0.0246 in that corpus but 0.1613 in the live post-R29 corpus), which then surfaces as a false driver and raises the mean live reading 19.5% -> 20.8%, closer to the 25% threshold. See observation_reports/r50.md A.3.
correction.the_defect_that_remains: STALENESS, not contamination, is this list's real problem, and it is NOT fixed here. R29 (2026-08-03) tripled crystallized-belief length: mean content tokens per document 9.6 pre-R29 vs 27.7 post. The current standing register is under-excluded -- 'aligns' (DF 0.1342) and 'discusses' (DF 0.1613) are in the live corpus at register-level frequency and appear in NO version of this list, which is why maxDF* now reads 18-24% with those as drivers. Fixing it needs ~1000 CLEAN POST-R29 documents; only 154 exist as of 2026-08-10, accruing ~78/day, so roughly 11 more clean days. Refit then, not before.
